title: Drinking Wine Has Lower Death Risk than Beer, Spirits
paragraphs: Drinking a lot of alcohol is bad for your health. But according to a large new study, the type of alcohol people drink may also make a difference, with wine linked to a lower risk of death than beer, cider and spirits.

The study was presented at a meeting of the American College of Cardiology in March 2026. Researchers led by Zhangling Chen, a professor at Central South University in China, used data from the UK Biobank, a large health database of British adults. They studied 340,924 people, who answered questions about what they ate and drank when they joined the study. The researchers then followed their health for more than 13 years on average. In their analysis, they took into account other factors, such as income, lifestyle and family medical history.

The researchers found that people who drank large amounts of alcohol, whatever the type, had a 24% higher risk of dying from any cause than people who never or only occasionally drank. Their risk of dying from cancer was 36% higher.

However, among people who drank low or moderate amounts, the results depended on the type of drink. Drinking spirits, beer or cider was linked to a significantly higher risk of death. For example, people who drank small amounts of these drinks had a 9% higher risk of dying from heart disease. On the other hand, the same amount of wine was linked to a lower risk of death. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of dying from heart disease.

The researchers suggested several possible reasons. Red wine contains substances such as polyphenols and antioxidants that may be good for the heart. Wine is also more often drunk with meals and by people who have healthier diets and lifestyles in general.

The researchers stressed that the study was observational, so it cannot prove that wine itself lowers the risk of death. Also, people in the UK Biobank are generally healthier than the population as a whole.
